**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — Apple pairs value-typed declarative `View` structs, modifier chains, and automatic Liquid Glass material adoption in [SwiftUI](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui) with [Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines) across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS, watchOS, tvOS, and iPhone Duo, while exposing structured actions, entities, `CardSnippet` views, and `SKILL.md` app skills to Apple Intelligence through [App Intents and the Siri AI Developer Preview](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents/siri-ai-developer-preview). It sets the gold standard for native Apple human-agent integration, but observed platform lock-in rules it out as a single cross-platform toolkit: there is no web or Android target, and Siri AI custom actions remain in Developer Preview (unavailable to App Store builds). An official web/cross-platform token and view bridge—or open MCP/HTTP export of compiled App Intents metadata—would address the ecosystem boundary.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — [Material Design 3 in Jetpack Compose](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3) combines `@Composable` functions, the fine-grained Compose Snapshot state runtime, `Modifier.Node` chains, M3 Expressive five-key tonal palettes, wallpaper-derived dynamic color, and adaptive window size classes across Android phones, foldables, XR, Cars, and Wear OS, alongside `androidx.a2ui.compose` and `material3-a2ui` for rendering agent-driven A2UI schemas natively without arbitrary code execution. While JetBrains Compose Multiplatform extends Compose beyond Android, Google's M3 Compose and A2UI artifacts remain Android-centric (`material3-a2ui` is still alpha), Compose on the web renders to canvas/WebAssembly rather than semantic HTML DOM—hindering browser-agent DOM and WebMCP inspection—and there is no built-in CLI/MCP action twin layer for deterministic screens. Semantic HTML output on web and graduating `androidx.a2ui.compose` alongside structured app-wide agent action contracts would address these trade-offs.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — [OpenAI Apps SDK UI](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui) (`@openai/apps-sdk-ui` v0.2.2 in [`package.json`](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui/blob/main/package.json)) is a lightweight React 18/19 library integrating Tailwind CSS v4 `@source` tokens, `radix-ui` primitives, router link injection via `AppsSDKUIProvider`, and 29 curated components (`Badge`, `Button`, `DateRangePicker`, `Markdown`, `ShimmerText`, `TagInput`) tailored for embedded ChatGPT Apps SDK surfaces. It does exactly what embedded ChatGPT cards need, but its observed scope is too narrow for a standalone cross-platform product: it has no native mobile renderers, omits full-application primitives like data tables, command palettes, and app shells, and lacks a host-independent runtime agent action protocol. Decoupling its token system from ChatGPT's host chrome, expanding its component catalog, and adding native mobile primitives would be required to use it outside conversational embeds.

**Ouro UI** — [Ouro UI](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui) explicitly splits the stack into human surfaces (**Ouro HX**: 110+ copy-in React 19, `@base-ui/react`, and Tailwind v4 components on web v1.3.14 plus SwiftUI `OuroHX` in [`ouro-ui-apple`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple)) and agent surfaces (**Ouro AX**: single-definition CLI/HTTP/MCP commands with `--why` and `--dry-run` safety gates, postcondition-checked `outcome()`, cursor `waitFor()`, Apple `App Intents`, and headless ~19ms screen driving via [`OuroReins`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple/blob/main/docs/ouro-reins/README.md)), unified by DTCG 2025.10 tokens and SHA-256-pinned claim sets in [`ouro-ui-core`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-core). Crucially, [`ax-component`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/main/docs/ax/ax-component.md) (`defineComponentAx` and `bindAx`) binds each UI component's readable state and allowed actions to CLI/MCP twins while enforcing `personOnly` reservations on mic/camera/screen controls, and `ouro-check`, `OuroFeel`, and `ax-xray` verify visual geometry, jank, accessibility, and black-box agent conformance without screenshot guessing. The concrete trade-offs are observed platform gaps and strictness: there is no Android or React Native target yet, `ouro-ui-apple` (`v0.3.x`) ships only five core `OuroHX` component families so far, `ax-mcp` is still a preview, and layout-only `className` rules disallow ad-hoc utility styling; shipping an Android Compose target from `ouro-ui-core`, expanding `ouro-ui-apple` to 1.0 parity, and stabilizing `ax-mcp` would close those gaps.

**Chakra UI** — Chakra UI v3 (`@chakra-ui/react` v3.38.0 in [`packages/react/package.json`](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/main/packages/react/package.json)) layers recipe and slot-recipe theming with `@emotion/react` over headless `@ark-ui/react` state machines with Next.js RSC support, and ships [`@chakra-ui/react-mcp`](https://chakra-ui.com/docs/get-started/ai/mcp-server), `llms.txt`, and AI Skills so coding assistants can query component props, tokens, and v2-to-v3 migrations. While productive for human-facing React web apps, it remains bound to React DOM and runtime Emotion CSS-in-JS with no native iOS or Android renderer, and its MCP server serves build-time coding agents rather than giving runtime agents structured state reads or action execution against rendered screens. Adding a cross-platform/native target without runtime CSS-in-JS overhead and exposing runtime agent action bindings on Ark state machines would address both limitations.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's [Fluent UI web monorepo](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui) centers on converged `@fluentui/react-components` v9—built with typed `slot.always`/`slot.optional` extensibility, `FluentProvider` CSS-variable tokens, and Griffel (`makeStyles`) atomic CSS-in-JS—alongside [`@fluentui/web-components`](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/blob/master/packages/web-components/README.md) with Declarative Shadow DOM SSR templates and a Custom Elements Manifest. It fits M365 and Teams surfaces well, but Fluent's native Apple, Android, and React Native libraries live in separate repositories with non-unified component APIs, Griffel's CSS-in-JS rules add friction for coding agents compared to standard CSS or Tailwind, and there is no built-in runtime agent action or generative UI layer. Unifying web and native packages around shared component contracts and exposing structured agent state/action metadata on slots would make it far stronger for cross-platform human-agent apps.

**Base UI** — [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start) (`@base-ui/react` v1.9.0) is a tree-shakeable, unstyled React primitive library from Radix, Floating UI, and MUI authors that replaces `Slot`/`asChild` cloning with a cleaner [`render` prop and `useRender` composition model](https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/composition) supporting multi-ref merging, `preventBaseUIHandler` event ordering, `isolation: isolate` portals, and `llms.txt` Markdown docs. Its primitive engineering is top-tier—which is why both `shadcn/ui` and `Ouro UI` build on it—but by design it stops at unstyled React DOM primitives, offering no design tokens, visual theme, native mobile targets, or runtime agent action/state bridge (and its focus-guard spans require explicit exclusions in `axe-core` audits). Pairing it with cross-platform tokens, pre-styled patterns, and explicit agent contracts—as Ouro UI does—addresses what Base UI intentionally omits.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Adobe's [React Spectrum monorepo](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum) cleanly separates `@internationalized/*` (30+ languages, 13 calendar systems), DOM-agnostic `react-stately` state hooks, 50+ unstyled [React Aria Components](https://react-aria.adobe.com/) with pointer/touch/screen-reader normalization, Spectrum 2 (`@react-spectrum/s2` using `@parcel/macros` compile-time styles), and [`@react-spectrum/ai`](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/main/packages/@react-spectrum/ai/exports/index.ts) (`Chat`, `PromptField`, `ExecutionTrace`, `ResponseStatus`), backed by MCP servers for coding assistants. Its web accessibility and internationalization are unmatched, yet despite `react-stately`'s platform-independent hooks, Adobe ships no official iOS, Android, or React Native views, `@react-spectrum/s2` ties styling to Parcel macros and Adobe's visual brand, and `@react-spectrum/ai` renders chat/trace widgets for humans without exposing a runtime bridge for agents to inspect or drive app controls. Official native renderers over `react-stately` and a runtime WebMCP/action layer on `react-aria-components` would address these gaps.

**A2UI** — [A2UI](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) ([v1.0 specification](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/)) is a streaming JSON generative UI protocol and [three-layer Core/Agent/Renderer SDK](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/) separating adjacency-list component graphs (`createSurface`, `updateComponents`) from reactive JSON Pointer state (`updateDataModel`), with schema-validated catalogs, bidirectional typed RPC (`callRendererFunction`/`callAgentFunction`), and native renderers across React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose (`v0.9.1`). It is the strongest open protocol for streaming untrusted or dynamic agent-generated views natively across platforms, but it is a wire protocol rather than a design system: v1.0 explicitly bans wire-level theme properties ("Decoupled Branding") so you must still bring a host design system, Jetpack Compose lags at v0.9.1, and it only models *agent-renders-UI-for-person* rather than giving agents a structured interface to operate deterministic app screens. Pairing A2UI with a full token/component design system and CLI/MCP action twins for static views would address what falls outside its protocol scope.

**Radix UI** — [Radix Primitives](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/overview/introduction) (`radix-ui` / `@radix-ui/react-*` from [`radix-ui/primitives`](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)) pioneered unstyled, open-part React web components handling WAI-ARIA roles, focus traps, roving tabindex, portals, controlled/uncontrolled state, and `Slot`/`asChild` element delegation. While foundational across the React web ecosystem, it is strictly DOM-only with no native mobile primitives or design tokens, leaves newer inputs (`Form`, `One-Time Password Field`, `Password Toggle Field`) in Preview while newer ecosystems migrate toward Base UI's `render` prop to avoid `asChild` prop/ref-forwarding friction, and includes no coding-agent or runtime-agent contract. Native cross-platform primitives, graduating form controls out of Preview, and exposing structured component state/action descriptors for agents would be needed to select it directly.

**Flutter** — [Flutter](https://docs.flutter.dev/resources/architectural-overview) compiles Dart `Widget` -> `Element` -> `RenderObject` trees to native ARM/x64 code and WebAssembly, rasterizing every pixel via its C++ Impeller/Skia engine across iOS, Android, desktop, and web with built-in Material and Cupertino catalogs plus the [GenUI SDK for Flutter](https://docs.flutter.dev/ai/genui) (`a2ui_flutter`) for JSON-driven agent widget composition. Its single-codebase native fidelity is compelling, but drawing to a GPU canvas on the web bypasses standard HTML DOM elements—degrading lightweight web delivery, native browser text/link ergonomics, and DOM/WebMCP inspection by browser agents—while `genui` remains experimental alpha and only covers agent-generated widgets for humans rather than programmatic agent operation of the app. First-class semantic DOM/WebMCP interoperability on web and stabilizing `genui` alongside headless app-driving primitives would address my main reservations.

**shadcn/ui** — [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs) combines open-code React + Tailwind CSS source ownership with a flat-file `registry.json` CLI, MCP server, project-aware Skills, three swappable v4 primitive bases (`base`, `aria`, and `radix` in [`bases.ts`](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/blob/main/apps/v4/registry/bases.ts)), and composable [`AI Elements`](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements) (`Trace`, `Reasoning`, `Tool`, `Confirmation`, `Message Scroller`). Its transparent code and predictable composition make it effortless for coding agents to read and customize on the web, which is why Ouro UI adopts its CLI/registry format. However, official `shadcn/ui` is strictly React DOM with no first-party iOS, Android, or React Native components or cross-platform token pipeline, ships no automated post-build visual/jank verifier, and its `AI Elements` only display agent output *to people* without giving runtime agents a permissioned action/state interface to use the app; official native registries and component-level runtime agent bindings would address both gaps.

**Tamagui** — [Tamagui](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui) ([v3 introduction](https://tamagui.dev/docs/intro/introduction)) unifies React web and React Native behind `@tamagui/core`, dual typed style-prop and `@tamagui/tailwind` frontends, `Adapt` responsive/platform presentation morphing, and `@tamagui/static`, a build-time compiler that flattens styled components into atomic CSS `div`s on web and hoisted `View`/`Text` styles on iOS and Android. Among pure UI kits, it offers the strongest React web-plus-native performance and code sharing, yet beyond `llms.txt` and setup prompts for coding agents, it has an observed gap on runtime agent use: there is no component-level state/action bridge, permission model, CLI/MCP/WebMCP twin layer, or generative UI catalog, alongside extra Metro/bundler compiler setup complexity. Adding a cross-platform runtime agent bridge over Tamagui components (exposing readable values, available choices, and guarded actions on both web and React Native) would address my biggest objection.

**MCP Apps** — [MCP Apps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) ([SEP-1865 `2026-01-26` stable spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx)) standardizes `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, linking MCP tools to `ui://` HTML resources (`text/html;profile=mcp-app`) rendered inside CSP-restricted sandboxed iframes across Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, and Goose with bidirectional JSON-RPC via `PostMessageTransport` and host theme syncing (`useHostStyles`). It solves cross-host tool UI delivery cleanly, but it is an iframe transport and sandboxing protocol rather than a design system—you still must bring your own component toolkit inside each HTML bundle, host feature support varies by client, and `text/html` iframes cannot deliver native SwiftUI/Compose controls or standalone full-application navigation. Standardized native view profiles beyond `text/html` and an official accessible component kit would help, though it remains a host-extension layer rather than an application design system.

**AI Elements** — [AI Elements](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements) provides copy-in React and Tailwind CSS-variable components (`Conversation`, `Message`, `CodeBlock`, `Reasoning`) built on `shadcn/ui` and `@ai-sdk/react` for Next.js chat interfaces. Its own README explicitly announces that `vercel/ai-elements` will be deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of [AI Elements in `shadcn/ui`](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements) (which also retires ~18 low-usage wrappers such as `artifact`, `canvas`, and `jsx-preview`), and even its successor patterns cover only web conversational display widgets for humans—not general application controls, native platforms, or interfaces operated by agents. Because the standalone project is being retired into `shadcn/ui`, new projects should not adopt this repository directly.

**json-render** — [json-render](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render) (`@json-render/core`) is a Zod-guardrailed Generative UI framework from Vercel Labs that compiles streaming element specs (`SpecStream`) with reactive `$state`, `$cond`, `$bindState`, and `watch` expressions across an extraordinary matrix of targets—including React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, `@json-render/shadcn`, `@json-render/react-native`, Next.js, TanStack Start, Ink TUIs, PDF, Email, Slack/Teams/Discord cards, Three.js, and `@json-render/mcp`. Its target breadth is unmatched for prompt-generated views, but as a `0.x` Labs spec compiler it is not a self-contained design system (visual tokens and accessibility depend on whichever target catalog you supply, with rich pre-built components mainly on web shadcn versus basic mobile definitions), and it models *agent-generates-UI-for-human* rather than *agent-uses-app* action postconditions and permissions. Reaching a stable 1.0 API with unified cross-platform design tokens and bidirectional agent-callable action contracts would address those gaps.

**Vercel UI SDK** — [Vercel UI SDK](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui) composes ARIA, focus, keyboard, selection, and popup behaviors in `@ui-sdk/core` (`definePrimitive`) into identical `createParts` components across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, paired with a live [agent bridge](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/agents/connect-an-agent) (`createAgent` exposing `snapshot`, `act` with `details.source === "agent"`, `query`, permissions, undo history, and [`registerTools` for browser `document.modelContext` WebMCP](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/agents/connect-an-agent/webmcp)). Its runtime `snapshot`/`act`/`query` + WebMCP architecture is arguably the cleanest browser-agent bridge in the field, but it is explicitly in public beta with unstable APIs, ships completely unstyled without design tokens or themes, and is strictly DOM-bound (`HTMLInputElement`, `packages/web`) with no native iOS, Android, or React Native targets. Graduating out of beta, pairing with a cross-platform token/theme layer, and extending `definePrimitive` + `createAgent` to native mobile would make it a top-tier choice.

**CopilotKit** — [CopilotKit](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit) connects agent backends (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Google ADK, or `BuiltInAgent`) over the event-driven `AG-UI` protocol to React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack/Teams (`Channels`), and WebMCP via `useAgent`, shared state, human-in-the-loop approvals, and [six generative UI primitives](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/concepts/generative-ui-overview) spanning Controlled (`useComponent`/`useRenderTool`), Declarative (A2UI 1.0), and Open-Ended (MCP Apps). It excels as an agent-user orchestration layer and copilot shell, but it is not a general-purpose design system for building an application's core buttons, forms, navigation, overlays, and tokens across web and native—you still must supply a separate UI toolkit—and production thread persistence, memories, and Slack/Teams hosting tie into CopilotKit Intelligence infrastructure. Coupling its `AG-UI` hooks with a first-party cross-platform component and token system would address the missing UI toolkit layer.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — [Agent-native](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native) (`@agent-native/core` v0.228.2) centers application architecture on [`defineAction()`](https://www.agent-native.com/docs/actions-overview/), automatically exposing each Zod-typed file in `actions/` simultaneously as React hooks (`useActionQuery`/`useActionMutation`), agent tools, HTTP endpoints, MCP tools, A2A tools, and CLI commands over a shared Drizzle/Postgres/PGlite database, alongside WebMCP, `/visual-edit` skills, and Expo/React Native (`uniwind`) mobile packages. Sharing one validated action layer between UI and agent eliminates backend drift cleanly, but it is an opinionated `0.x` full-stack Nitro + SQL application framework rather than a portable design system or UI toolkit that can drop into existing web, SwiftUI, or Android apps. Decoupling its UI components, design tokens, and client-side action bindings into a standalone, framework-agnostic 1.0 UI package would address that architectural lock-in.

**MUI** — [Material UI](https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/) (`@mui/material` v9.5.0, with v10 alpha in [`packages/mui-material/package.json`](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/packages/mui-material/package.json)) offers a deeply battle-tested React component catalog extended by MUI X, supporting `@emotion/react` alongside optional zero-runtime `@mui/material-pigment-css` extraction, CSS theme variables, `llms.txt`, and [`@mui/mcp`](https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/mcp/) documentation tools for coding assistants. Despite its vast web component breadth, it remains React DOM-only with no native mobile renderer, still implements Material Design 2 by default per its current v9 overview docs, splits advanced data components across commercial MUI X tiers, and limits AI support to build-time documentation lookup with no runtime agent state or action surface. Native cross-platform token/component support, Material 3 / neutral design refresh, and runtime agent action hooks would be required to choose it here.

actions.testimonial: I would choose Ouro UI because it treats human interfaces (Ouro HX) and agent interfaces (Ouro AX) as peers backed by the same DTCG 2025.10 tokens and byte-verified claim sets in ouro-ui-core. Instead of forcing agents to scrape pixels or guess props, defineComponentAx and bindAx bind each rendered control to explicit CLI, MCP, or App Intents twins—enforcing consent gates and person-only boundaries on sensitive controls like cameras and microphones—while OuroReins lets agents drive native SwiftUI screens headlessly as JSON state and actions in milliseconds. For coding agents and humans alike, ouro-check, OuroFeel, and ax-xray verify accessibility, layout geometry, interaction jank, and black-box agent conformance automatically without relying on brittle screenshot inspection. The honest trade-off versus Tamagui or Flutter is native platform breadth today: Ouro UI has no Android target yet and its Apple SwiftUI package (v0.3.x) ships far fewer components than its 110-plus React web registry, so teams needing immediate Android parity must bridge that gap until core's token and claim pipeline expands there.
